# Corridor mask runner contacts and near whistle

Two actual human whistle candidates are retained with original high quality
public MP3 preview bytes and hashes. Lunardrive's short male lip whistle has a
dry defined start and mouth detail; jperezjacome's tongue/front-teeth whistle
has an airy panflute-like timbre. The final near warning combines brief excerpts
from both into three uneven gestures. Both sources are CC0. The sound is edited
performed whistling, with source delays and rate/filter edits, never an invented
oscillator effect. A full melody was avoided so the result reads as a creature
signal rather than music.

The original corridor parquet heel contacts were compared with the existing
physical workshop plank clap and dropped metal contact. Shoe-only contacts are
too light for the very large runner; the selected mix preserves distinct shoe
contacts while the low plank and metal body supply weight. Three actual parquet
contacts remain distinct. Runtime footsteps depend on real NavMesh travel.
The same retained workshop originals create one actual door-break cue.

Rebuild with `SourceArt/Audio/render_corridor_mask.py` and
`requirements-corridor.txt`. Existing source manifests own the parquet and
workshop recordings; this package does not duplicate their originals. All
transformations and source origin hashes are in the canonical manifest.

No candidate or result was played through a speaker during automated authoring.
PCM and runtime DSP checks demonstrate data and lifecycle behavior, not human
listening quality. The ordinary game retains its configured volume; diagnostic
players use the current-process Windows silence guard before testing native DSP.
